themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste & Outdoor Dining Chaos
themes_detail.summary: Commercial Disposal complaints spiked 2300% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average) and Outdoor Dining complaints surged 1500% (4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average), suggesting a potential enforcement gap or sudden increase in unpermitted commercial activity in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens.
evidence: Commercial Disposal: 3 complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
Outdoor Dining: 4 complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66)
Both spikes registered this week with extreme statistical significance
reporting_angles: Have restaurants or food vendors recently been granted new outdoor permits or operating without proper licensing?
Is Sanitation enforcement stretched thin or changing enforcement priorities in the district?

themes_detail.label: Street & Curb Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb Condition complaints surged 408% THIS WEEK (33 complaints vs. 6.5 weekly average, z-score 6.25), and Dead/Dying Tree complaints jumped 433% (6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 average), pointing to widespread pavement and streetscape neglect affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: Curb Condition: 33 complaints this week vs. 6.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.25, severity: high)
Dead/Dying Tree: 6 complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.63, severity: high)
Street Condition remains top 5 complaint overall (567 in 90 days), now accelerating
reporting_angles: Which streets are seeing the most curb damage—are these potholes, broken pavers, or drainage issues?
Is tree mortality linked to recent weather, pest activity, or deferred maintenance in Parks?

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Illegal Encampments Rise
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped 243% THIS WEEK (12 vs. 3.5 weekly average, z-score 5.13), and Encampment complaints surged 380% LAST WEEK (9 vs. 1.9 average, z-score 4.21), suggesting a sharp increase in street blockages and homeless encampments that aligns with repeated CB budget requests for homeless services.
evidence: Obstruction: 12 complaints this week vs. 3.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.13, severity: high)
Encampment: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.21, severity: high)
Community Board has submitted repeated annual requests for 'services for the homeless' to Department of Homeless Services
reporting_angles: Where are encampments clustering—Prospect Park perimeter, Gowanus Canal waterfront, or residential blocks?
Are DHS outreach teams deployed in Park Slope, and what do residents say about response times?

themes_detail.label: Vendor & Street Enforcement Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints spiked 540% THIS WEEK (4 complaints vs. 0.6 weekly average, z-score 4.85), suggesting either a sudden surge in unlicensed street vending or a shift in enforcement operations—worth investigating whether this is supply-side (new vendors) or demand-side (stricter enforcement).
evidence: Vendor Enforcement: 4 complaints this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.85, severity: high)
Spike coincides with Commercial Disposal and Outdoor Dining spikes, suggesting coordinated street commerce activity
reporting_angles: Is the city running a new enforcement sweep against street vendors in Park Slope, or are residents reporting more unlicensed vendors?
Are food carts, ice cream trucks, or other vendors clustering in particular neighborhoods within the district?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike Three Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Drug Activity complaints surged 700% THREE WEEKS AGO (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score 5.42), representing a persistent safety concern, though the spike is no longer THIS WEEK and may have stabilized or resolved.
evidence: Drug Activity: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, severity: high)
Timing: spike is dated but worth follow-up to determine if activity persists or was episodic
reporting_angles: Has drug activity resolved since the spike three weeks ago, or is it ongoing and underreported?
Are there specific blocks or parks where residents report concentrated activity?
